steps.intent: The Russian Federation’s objective is to secure a short, time-bound six-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism while reinforcing respect for Syria’s sovereignty, strengthening cross-line deliveries, and ensuring transparency, monitoring, and a review of the mechanism’s effectiveness. The main difficulty will be overcoming Western pressure for a longer, unconditional extension and persuading at least one of the abstaining elected members—particularly Malta or Switzerland—to support the draft, while maintaining a unified position among like-minded Council members. The text therefore emphasizes humanitarian access and a clear review clause to attract the nine votes needed without provoking a veto.
steps.text:
The Security Council,
Recalling all its previous relevant resolutions and statements of its President concerning the Syrian Arab Republic, including resolutions 2642 (2022) and 2672 (2023),
Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,
Reaffirming also the primary responsibility of the Syrian authorities to protect the population in Syria and to ensure the provision of humanitarian assistance,
Recalling the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and the need for all parties to respect them,
Expressing grave concern at the continuing dire humanitarian situation in Syria, including the impact of the devastating earthquake of 6 February 2023 and the ongoing displacement, food insecurity, and lack of access to basic services, and the need for a sustained and scaled-up humanitarian response,
Stressing the need for unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access to all people in need in Syria through all modalities, including cross-line and cross-border, in accordance with international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles,
Noting the need to ensure the transparency and effectiveness of humanitarian assistance, including the timely and independent monitoring of the delivery and distribution of aid, and to prevent the diversion of humanitarian assistance to terrorist groups,
Reaffirming that the cross-border mechanism is a temporary measure to address the urgent humanitarian needs of the civilian population and should be complemented by strengthened cross-line deliveries,
Welcoming the efforts of the United Nations and its humanitarian partners, and the cooperation of the Syrian authorities in facilitating humanitarian access,
Noting the reports of the Secretary-General on the humanitarian situation in Syria,
Determining that the situation in Syria continues to constitute a threat to international peace and security,
Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,
1. Decides to renew until 10 January 2024 the authorization for United Nations humanitarian agencies and their implementing partners to use the Bab al-Hawa crossing for the delivery of humanitarian assistance into Syria, as set out in the relevant provisions of resolutions 2642 (2022) and 2672 (2023);
2. Requests the Secretary-General to continue to report to the Security Council on a monthly basis on the humanitarian situation in Syria, including on the implementation of this resolution, the effectiveness of cross-line deliveries, the needs assessment process, and the measures taken to ensure the transparency and monitoring of humanitarian assistance and to prevent its diversion;
3. Calls upon all parties to the conflict to ensure safe, unhindered and sustained access for humanitarian actors to all areas of Syria, through cross-line and cross-border modalities, in accordance with international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles;
4. Demands that all parties comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law, including the protection of civilians and civilian objects, and refrain from any action that may impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance;
5. Requests the Secretary-General to conduct a review of the implementation of this resolution after six months and to report to the Council on whether the cross-border mechanism should be further extended, taking into account the humanitarian needs, the effectiveness of cross-line deliveries, and the overall situation in Syria;
6. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

Add an operative paragraph demanding that all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, remove arbitrary restrictions and facilitate safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access to all people in need through all modalities.

Brazil.change: Replace 'after six months' with 'after nine months'.

Add: 'Calls for the lifting of all unilateral coercive measures against Syria, which exacerbate the humanitarian situation and impede the humanitarian response, and stresses that humanitarian assistance should not be politicized.'

Replace 'on whether the cross-border mechanism should be further extended' with 'on progress in scaling up cross-line deliveries and on the orderly transition to cross-line delivery as the main channel, with a view to the eventual termination of the cross-border mechanism.'

Replace the review clause with a request for the Secretary-General to report after six months on implementation of this resolution, without implying that the authorization expires or is conditioned on a further decision before the end of the 12-month period.

Replace 'whether the cross-border mechanism should be further extended' with 'the humanitarian needs and the implementation of this resolution, and expresses its intention to renew the authorization in a timely manner'.
Insert after 'monitoring of the delivery and distribution of aid' the phrase 'in a manner consistent with humanitarian principles and without impeding humanitarian operations'.

Delete the six-month review clause and replace it with: 'Requests the Secretary-General to report to the Council on the implementation of this resolution no later than 10 March 2024, without prejudice to the renewal of the authorization in paragraph 1.'

Japan.change: Replace 'and the cooperation of the Syrian authorities in facilitating humanitarian access' with 'and calls upon the Syrian authorities to facilitate rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all areas of Syria'.

messages.Albania: Albania supports renewing the cross-border lifeline, but cannot accept a six-month, single-crossing text that again leaves aid vulnerable to political conditions. We ask the penholder to extend OP1 for 12 months and cover Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai, and to revise OP5 so that the authorization is not made contingent on a review linked to cross-line deliveries. We also need a clear operative demand that the Syrian authorities and all parties remove arbitrary restrictions on humanitarian access.
messages.Brazil: Brazil welcomes the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization, which is essential to address the dire humanitarian situation. However, a six-month extension is too short to provide predictability and ensure sustained operations. We ask for a nine-month extension until 10 April 2024, with the review clause adjusted accordingly. We also stress that monitoring must not impede humanitarian access and that cross-line and cross-border deliveries should be complementary.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the renewal of the cross-border mechanism and appreciates the Russian Federation's efforts to find a compromise. We believe the text should be strengthened to ensure predictable, needs-based humanitarian access for all Syrians in need. We therefore ask for a 12-month extension, explicit access to all areas including those not under government control, and language ensuring that monitoring and counter-diversion measures do not impede humanitarian action. We also suggest that reporting include impediments to access and the views of humanitarian actors.
messages.France: France thanks the Russian Federation for the draft and supports renewal of the cross-border mechanism. However, a six-month renewal is inadequate given the scale of humanitarian needs, including after the earthquake; France cannot accept anything less than a 12-month authorization. We also call for the authorization to cover the Bab al-Salam and Bab al-Rai crossings, and for the six-month review not to condition the mandate. France remains committed to resolution 2254 (2015) and to ensuring assistance reaches all Syrians in need.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa authorization to avoid a humanitarian gap, but the current six-month duration is too short given the scale of needs. We ask that OP1 be extended to nine months, until 10 April 2024, and that OP5 not condition continuation on cross-line benchmarks. We also seek a safeguard that monitoring and transparency measures do not impede humanitarian access and are developed with UN humanitarian agencies.
messages.Ghana: Ghana thanks the Russian Federation for circulating the draft and supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa authorization. We ask that the renewal be longer and more predictable, that the authorization cover all available cross-border crossings, and that the six-month review not be framed as a default expiry. With those changes, Ghana can support the text.
messages.Japan: Japan cannot support the current text as drafted. The six-month, single-crossing authorization and the open-ended review clause fall short of the humanitarian needs; we need at least a nine-month extension including Bab al-Salam, and reporting that does not condition renewal. We also ask that praise for the Syrian authorities be removed and that monitoring be explicitly UN-led, consistent with humanitarian principles.
messages.Malta: Malta thanks the Russian Federation for circulating this draft and supports a timely renewal of the cross-border mechanism to prevent further humanitarian deterioration. We could support the text with the following changes: OP1 should authorize the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings until at least 10 April 2024, and OP5 should base any review on humanitarian needs and the Secretary-General's recommendations rather than cross-line benchmarks. We also ask that the monitoring and reporting language in OP2 explicitly safeguard humanitarian principles and unimpeded access.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization for six months and welcomes the draft's emphasis on humanitarian access, cross-line deliveries, and the prevention of diversion to terrorist groups. We consider the text to be a balanced basis for avoiding a humanitarian gap and are ready to support it as it stands. We encourage the penholder to continue engaging all Council members to ensure the resolution's adoption.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks the Russian Federation for the draft and supports the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, which remains a lifeline for millions in north-west Syria. We ask for a nine-month extension to give humanitarian actors predictability, and we request the deletion of OP5, which introduces unnecessary conditionality. We also seek language ensuring that monitoring and transparency measures are carried out in full respect of humanitarian principles and do not impede access. We are ready to engage constructively to secure a unanimous adoption.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the renewal of the cross-border mechanism to prevent any interruption in life-saving assistance, and we thank the Russian Federation for its efforts. We ask that the authorization be extended for nine months, until 10 April 2024, and include the Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings as needed to reach all affected areas. The text should also reflect the importance of scaling up cross-line deliveries and early recovery projects, including electricity, water, sanitation, health and demining, in line with resolution 2672 (2023). We are ready to engage constructively to reach consensus.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the Russian Federation for circulating this draft and can support the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism. However, we strongly believe the Council must provide a 12-month mandate to give the humanitarian community the operational certainty it has repeatedly requested. We also ask that OP5 reflect the Council's clear intention to renew, rather than leaving the mechanism conditional on a review, and that any monitoring be consistent with humanitarian principles.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a text that retreats to a single crossing and a six-month horizon; we need the authorization to preserve Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai and to provide predictable access for at least a full year. We also want reporting on use of all authorized crossings and no review clause that could undermine the renewal. We are ready to work with the penholder to adjust these points.

replies.Brazil: partially accepted: duration extended to 12 months, exceeding nine-month request; review reporting retained at six months with safeguards.
replies.China: partially accepted: cross-line transition and UCM language added, but no full plan for termination or unconditional lifting of coercive measures.
replies.Ecuador: accepted: 12-month renewal, explicit access to areas not under government control, reporting details, and monitoring safeguards included.
replies.France: partially accepted: 12-month renewal and all three crossings authorized, but two crossings include Syrian consultation; 2254 reference added.
replies.Gabon: partially accepted: 12-month renewal exceeds nine months; reporting and monitoring safeguards included, but review retained without conditionality.
replies.Ghana: partially accepted: 12-month renewal and all three crossings included with qualifier; reporting and monitoring safeguards incorporated.
replies.Japan: partially accepted: duration and crossings exceed request; cooperation language softened and monitoring safeguard added, but not UN-led.
replies.Malta: partially accepted: 12-month renewal and three crossings included with qualifier; review based on needs and recommendations partially reflected.
replies.Mozambique: accepted: no changes requested; core renewal maintained.
replies.Switzerland: partially accepted: nine-month request exceeded with 12 months; OP5 conditionality removed but reporting/review retained; monitoring safeguards added.
replies.United Arab Emirates: partially accepted: nine-month request exceeded; Bab al-Salam/Al-Rai with Syrian consultation included; early recovery reflected in reporting, not separate OP.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: 12-month authorization and six-month reporting included; review without prejudice to authorization.
replies.United States of America: partially accepted: all three crossings and 12-month renewal included, but two crossings include Syrian consultation; reporting on use of crossings added.

steps.summary: The revised text extends the cross-border authorization for 12 months, includes all three crossings with Syrian consultation for two, and adds cross-line transition, monitoring safeguards, and humanitarian access language. It is designed to secure broad Council support while preserving key Russian priorities on Syrian sovereignty and cross-line assistance.

messages.Albania: Albania appreciates the 12-month renewal and inclusion of Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai, but we cannot accept a text that makes two of the three crossings dependent on Syrian authorities' consent. We also need the cross-border authorization to remain a standing channel, not a temporary arrangement to be replaced by cross-line delivery, and a clear call on the Syrian authorities to remove arbitrary access restrictions. With those changes, Albania is ready to support the draft.
messages.Brazil: Brazil welcomes the 12-month renewal and the safeguards on monitoring, and can support the text. However, we cannot accept language that makes use of Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai contingent on the Syrian authorities, nor that frames cross-border aid as merely transitional to cross-line delivery as the main channel. With these two adjustments, Brazil is ready to vote in favour.
messages.China: China supports the Russian draft as a basis and appreciates the incorporation of cross-line transition and unilateral coercive measures language. To ensure the cross-border mechanism remains temporary and fully respects Syria's sovereignty, China requests a clear timetable and eventual termination in OP5, together with a 90-day plan for scaling up cross-line deliveries. China also asks for stronger language in OP6 calling for the lifting of unilateral coercive measures. We hope these concerns can be accommodated so that the Council can maintain unity and China can support the text.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador welcomes the penholder's incorporation of the 12-month renewal, explicit access to areas not under government control, and strengthened reporting and monitoring. We can support the text with clarifications that cross-line efforts strengthen, rather than condition or replace, the cross-border authorization in OP1. These changes would preserve the humanitarian and needs-based character of the mechanism and allow Ecuador to join consensus.
messages.France: France supports renewing the cross-border mechanism for 12 months and welcomes the authorization of all three crossings. However, we cannot accept a mechanism whose operation is subject to consultation with the Syrian authorities, nor language that makes cross-line delivery the main channel and thereby undermines the cross-border authorization. We also oppose OP6 as drafted, which calls into question the sanctions regime; it must be deleted or replaced with a humanitarian-exemptions formulation.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the revised draft as a balanced compromise that renews the cross-border humanitarian mechanism for twelve months and incorporates necessary monitoring and transparency safeguards. We appreciate the penholder's efforts to reflect humanitarian principles and to retain reporting without conditioning the authorization. We urge all Council members to support the text so that life-saving assistance can continue to reach millions of Syrians in need.
messages.Ghana: Ghana welcomes the 12-month renewal and the inclusion of all three crossings, and we can support the text with these refinements. Cross-line delivery should be needs-based and complementary to the cross-border authorization, not framed as the 'main channel' in a way that prejudges OP1. We also seek to clarify in OP1 that consultation with the Syrian authorities does not become a precondition and that UN humanitarian actors are consulted.
messages.Japan: Japan welcomes the longer renewal and the inclusion of Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai. However, additional crossings must not be conditional on the Syrian authorities, and the text should not frame cross-border delivery as a temporary step toward cross-line delivery as the main channel. We also ask that the review clause not become an early termination mechanism and that monitoring be UN-led; Japan will engage constructively to preserve humanitarian access.
messages.Malta: Malta welcomes the 12-month renewal and the inclusion of the three crossings, but the qualifier in OP1 leaves humanitarian access subject to Syrian authorities and should be removed. We also cannot accept language in OP5 and OP7 that makes cross-line delivery the main channel; cross-border assistance must remain needs-based and complementary. With those adjustments, Malta is ready to support the text.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism as contained in revision 1. We welcome the emphasis on sovereignty, humanitarian principles, and the need to address unilateral coercive measures. We encourage the Council to unite behind this text to ensure unimpeded humanitarian access to all Syrians in need.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the 12-month renewal and the monitoring safeguards in OP2, which respond to our concerns. We can support the text if OP1 does not make the Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings contingent on consultation with the Syrian authorities; humanitarian access must be needs-based and coordinated with UN humanitarian actors. We also ask that OP5 and OP7 remove language envisaging a transition to cross-line delivery as the main channel, replacing it with a needs-based, complementary approach without prejudice to the OP1 authorization.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE welcomes the renewal through 10 July 2024 and the inclusion of Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai in consultation with the Syrian authorities. We continue to believe that early recovery must be operationalized, not only reported on, particularly electricity, water, sanitation, health and education facilities, and demining. We therefore request a separate operative paragraph to that effect, respecting Syria's sovereignty and humanitarian principles; with that addition, we are ready to support the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK welcomes the 12-month renewal and six-month reporting, which are essential for operational certainty. However, we cannot accept language that subordinates the cross-border authorization to a transition to cross-line delivery as the main channel or gives the Syrian authorities a veto over additional crossings. We also oppose calls to ease unilateral coercive measures and ask that the sanctions language be reframed around humanitarian exemptions. With these changes, we can support the text.
messages.United States of America: We welcome the 12-month renewal and the inclusion of all three crossings. We cannot accept conditioning Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai on consultation with the Syrian authorities; cross-border access must be authorized by this Council, not Damascus. We also need OP5 and OP7 to focus on scaling up cross-line deliveries based on humanitarian needs rather than prescribing a transition, and OP6 on unilateral coercive measures should be deleted. With those changes, we are prepared to support the text.

replies.Albania: partially accepted: OP1 authorizes all three crossings without Syrian consent, but OP3 does not single out the Syrian authorities.
replies.China: partially accepted: cross-line scaling-up retained, but no 90-day termination plan or call to lift unilateral coercive measures.
replies.Ghana: partially accepted: transition language removed and complementarity added, but OP1 does not include consultation with Syrian authorities.
replies.Switzerland: partially accepted: Syrian consent removed and UN coordination added, but no explicit 'as needed' qualifier.

steps.summary: The revision removes Syrian consent as a condition for the Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings, recasts cross-line delivery as complementary rather than a transition to a main channel, and reframes sanctions language around humanitarian exemptions. It retains Russian priorities on sovereignty, monthly reporting, and early recovery, while dropping the operative call on unilateral coercive measures to secure P5 support.

reasons.Albania: Albania’s red line on authorizing all three crossings without Syrian consent was met, and despite remaining concerns over OP3, the humanitarian imperative and its record support a yes vote.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil’s red-line and important requests were accepted, and the amended text preserves cross-border humanitarian access while ensuring complementarity with cross-line aid, consistent with Brazil’s humanitarian priorities. Therefore Brazil votes in favour.
reasons.China: China supports the Russian draft as it aligns with its position on Syrian sovereignty and cross-line aid, despite unaccepted amendments; voting in favour maintains Council unity and supports an ally, while the statement records China's concerns.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador has consistently supported the humanitarian cross-border renewal, and its two important requested changes on cross-line language were accepted. It therefore votes in favour.
reasons.France: France supports the 12-month renewal and authorization of all three crossings, which align with its humanitarian priorities, despite concerns over early recovery language. It votes yes to sustain vital cross-border aid while dissociating from any political normalization.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon had already stated support, made no requests, and consistently favours humanitarian renewals that preserve access and sovereignty. The draft reflects those priorities, so Gabon casts a favourable vote.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana’s key requested changes on complementarity and non-prejudice were partially accepted, addressing its main concerns, and Ghana has consistently supported renewals of cross-border humanitarian access. It therefore votes in favour while emphasizing humanitarian principles, monitoring and unimpeded access.
reasons.Japan: Japan’s established policy supports renewing the Syria cross-border humanitarian mechanism, and the draft contains key safeguards Japan sought. Voting in favour is consistent with Japan’s prior votes and humanitarian priorities.
reasons.Malta: Malta has consistently supported humanitarian renewals on Syria and had its red-line amendment accepted by the penholder. The revised text preserves cross-border access while retaining safeguards, so Malta votes yes.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique had already indicated support with no requested changes, reflecting its priority on humanitarian access and respect for Syrian sovereignty. Voting in favour is consistent with its prior humanitarian resolutions on Syria and its non-confrontational Council posture.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation submitted this draft and would vote in favour of its own balanced humanitarian text, explaining its position before the vote. This aligns with its stated emphasis on Syrian sovereignty, non-politicization, cross-line delivery and anti-terrorist safeguards.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland prioritizes sustained cross-border humanitarian access and the draft renews the mechanism while partially accommodating its key concerns; despite remaining textual concerns, it aligns with Switzerland's humanitarian and principled position.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE has consistently supported renewals of UN humanitarian access to Syria while prioritizing sovereignty and early recovery; its requested amendment on early recovery was accepted, so it backs the Russian draft. This also aligns with its recorded vote in favour of the Russian draft on 11 July 2023.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft meets the UK's red lines: a 12-month renewal of all three crossings, no Syrian Government consent requirement, and cross-line deliveries as complementary rather than a substitute. Despite some concerns about OP6, the humanitarian imperative and the UK's consistent record support a yes vote.
reasons.United States of America: The final text meets the U.S. red line by authorizing all three crossings without Syrian regime consent and removes problematic language on early recovery and transition to cross-line as the main channel. Supporting this compromise secures a twelve-month humanitarian lifeline while preserving U.S. insistence on unhindered access.

before.Albania: Albania will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the authorization of the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings for the full period, without prior consent by the Syrian authorities, as this is essential for predictable humanitarian access. While we regret that not all of our concerns were fully reflected, in particular the explicit call on the Syrian authorities to remove arbitrary restrictions, Albania supports the renewal in view of the urgent humanitarian needs of the Syrian people and calls on all parties to ensure unimpeded, principled and sustained humanitarian access.
before.Brazil: Brazil will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us. We welcome the incorporation of our proposals, which ensure that cross-border and cross-line deliveries are considered on the basis of humanitarian needs and remain complementary, without prejudicing the authorized crossings. The renewal of the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings is essential to reach millions of Syrians in need. We stress that humanitarian access must be guided by the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and must not be politicized. Brazil remains committed to working with all Council members to sustain and scale up the humanitarian response in Syria.
before.China: Mr. President, China supports the draft resolution and will vote in favour. We thank the Russian Federation for its efforts. China has consistently maintained that humanitarian assistance to Syria should respect Syria's sovereignty and the ownership of the Syrian Government. Cross-border delivery is a temporary arrangement under special circumstances and should be gradually transitioned to cross-line delivery as the main channel. We welcome the draft's emphasis on scaling up cross-line assistance and early recovery. At the same time, we regret that our proposals for a clear timetable for the eventual termination of the cross-border mechanism and for lifting unilateral coercive measures were not fully reflected. We continue to believe that unilateral sanctions exacerbate the humanitarian situation and should be lifted. We call upon all parties to ensure safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access to all people in need. Thank you.
before.Ecuador: Mr. President, Ecuador thanks the Russian Federation for its efforts and appreciates that our requested amendments were taken into account. The humanitarian situation in Syria, including the impact of the February earthquake, requires sustained, predictable and unimpeded access through all modalities, in accordance with the humanitarian principles. We welcome the renewal of the authorization for the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings, and we underline that cross-line deliveries should be strengthened based on humanitarian needs, complement and not substitute for cross-border access, and should not condition that access. We also stress the importance of transparent United Nations-led monitoring, protection of civilians, and respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. For these reasons, Ecuador will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.France: (spoke in French): France welcomes the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism for 12 months and the authorization of the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings. This responds to the immense humanitarian needs of the Syrian people, particularly after the devastating earthquake. France will vote in favour. We stress that cross-line deliveries must complement, not substitute for, cross-border assistance. Early recovery activities must be strictly humanitarian, needs-based and neutral, and must not prejudge the political process or constitute normalization with the Syrian regime. France remains committed to resolution 2254 (2015) and to the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Syria.
before.Gabon: Gabon thanks the penholder for its efforts and will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism is essential to meet the urgent needs of millions of Syrians, and we stress that humanitarian assistance must remain impartial, humanitarian, and UN-led, while respecting Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We call on all parties to protect civilians, remove impediments to access, and facilitate both cross-border and cross-line deliveries in accordance with international humanitarian law.
before.Ghana: Thank you, Mr. President. Ghana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the Russian Federation for its efforts and all delegations for their constructive engagement. In the light of the devastating humanitarian situation in Syria, including the impact of the February earthquake, the Council must preserve unimpeded, sustained and principled humanitarian access to all people in need through both cross-border and cross-line modalities. We welcome that the text now clearly reflects that cross-line deliveries complement, and do not substitute for, the cross-border authorization, and that implementation is to be reviewed on the basis of humanitarian needs and without prejudice to that authorization. We also underline the importance of transparency, independent and United Nations-led monitoring, respect for humanitarian principles, and ensuring that assistance reaches those most in need without politicization. We urge all parties to facilitate safe and unhindered humanitarian access and to comply with international humanitarian law. Ghana remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and to a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under resolution 2254. For these reasons, Ghana votes in favour.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the cross-border mechanism is a lifeline for millions of civilians, especially in north-west Syria. We welcome the renewal of the authorized crossings until 10 July 2024, the provisions on United Nations-led monitoring and transparency, and the emphasis that cross-border deliveries must complement, and not be substituted by, cross-line assistance. Japan calls on all parties to ensure safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access, to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and to comply with international humanitarian law. We also stress that humanitarian assistance must remain impartial, needs-based and free from politicization.
before.Malta: Thank you, Mr. President. Malta will vote in favour of this draft. We do so because the humanitarian needs in Syria remain grave, and the renewal of authorized crossings alongside strengthened cross-line deliveries is essential to reaching civilians in need. We welcome that the penholder accepted Malta’s proposed changes, which preserve humanitarian access while ensuring that cross-line delivery complements, rather than substitutes for, cross-border assistance. We also stress that monitoring must be independent, UN-led and must never be used to impede principled humanitarian action.
before.Mozambique: Mozambique votes in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria, including the consequences of the February earthquake, requires sustained and predictable humanitarian access to all people in need. We support the renewal of the authorized crossings while stressing that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and must be implemented in full respect of humanitarian principles, including neutrality, impartiality and independence. Mozambique underscores the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and calls on all parties to facilitate safe, unhindered and sustained access, including through strengthened cross-line deliveries, and to protect civilians and civilian objects.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation has submitted this draft resolution because the humanitarian situation in Syria requires a pragmatic, balanced and non-politicized response. Our text preserves the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, while ensuring that United Nations humanitarian agencies can continue to deliver assistance through the authorized crossings in accordance with international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles. It also strengthens cross-line deliveries, early recovery and transparency, including monitoring to prevent the diversion of aid to terrorist groups. We call on all Council members to support this balanced text, which addresses urgent humanitarian needs without undermining Syria’s sovereignty or prejudging the political process.
before.Switzerland: Mr. President, Switzerland will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of the United Nations cross-border humanitarian mechanism through the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings until 10 July 2024. At a time when millions of Syrians depend on this lifeline, the Council must ensure that humanitarian access is not interrupted. We note that some of our proposals have been reflected, in particular that the authorization is coordinated with United Nations humanitarian agencies and that cross-line deliveries must complement, not substitute for, cross-border access. However, we regret that an explicit "as needed" reference and clearer complementary language were not fully retained. Switzerland supports the text on the understanding that all modalities will be implemented in full respect of humanitarian principles and international humanitarian law, without politicization, and that the authorization remains effective until its expiry. We call on all parties to facilitate rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel.
before.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of the draft before us. Our vote reflects the urgent need to sustain and scale up humanitarian access to all Syrians through both cross-border and cross-line modalities. We welcome the incorporation of our proposal on early recovery, including the restoration of electricity, water, sanitation, health and education facilities, which is essential to alleviating the suffering of the Syrian people. At the same time, we stress that humanitarian assistance must be delivered in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, with effective monitoring to prevent diversion, and must not be politicized. We call on all parties to facilitate rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and to place the needs of the Syrian people above political considerations.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. It renews the United Nations cross-border humanitarian mechanism for twelve months, authorises the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings, and affirms that cross-line deliveries must complement, not substitute for, this lifeline. We welcome the removal of any requirement for Syrian Government consent for the additional crossings and the assurance that the six-month review will not prejudice the twelve-month authorization. The humanitarian needs of the Syrian people must remain our sole guide. We urge all parties to ensure safe, unhindered and sustained access, and we stress that sanctions must not impede humanitarian action. The United Kingdom calls on all members to support this resolution.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the renewal of authorization for United Nations humanitarian agencies and their partners to use the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings for a further twelve months. This is a lifeline for millions of Syrians, and it must not be conditioned on the approval of the Syrian regime. We appreciate that the text now reflects the need for all three crossings and stresses that cross-line deliveries must complement, not substitute for, cross-border assistance. We remain deeply concerned by the Assad regime’s obstruction of humanitarian access and will continue to insist on unhindered, principled delivery to all Syrians in need. The Council must not politicize humanitarian assistance.

after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation, as penholder, thanks all members of the Council for their constructive engagement and for supporting this balanced draft. Its unanimous adoption demonstrates that the Council is able to act pragmatically when it proceeds from the real humanitarian needs of the Syrian people and respects the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

Our text preserves the principles of humanitarian assistance and does not politicize it. It ensures that United Nations humanitarian agencies and their implementing partners can continue to use the authorized crossings while strengthening cross-line deliveries, early recovery projects and transparent United Nations-led monitoring to prevent the diversion of assistance to terrorist groups. At the same time, we stress that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and exceptional and cannot become a substitute for assistance delivered in accordance with Syrian sovereignty and in coordination with the Syrian Government.

We note that not all our concerns were fully reflected, including on clearer benchmarks for the transition to cross-line delivery and on the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures. The Russian Federation will continue to follow the implementation of this resolution closely. We call on all parties to ensure safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access, to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and to avoid any attempts to use humanitarian assistance as an instrument of political pressure. The Russian Federation remains committed to supporting the Syrian people and to a political settlement on the basis of resolution 2254 (2015).
